declaration.negotiation_history_statement: Whitcombe Reyes LLP and Brightline’s counsel negotiated the settlement over three rounds. We initially proposed a $32 million class fund with automatic payments to identified members, plus up to $2 million in court-approved fees and expenses. Brightline countered with a $27 million fund on the same distribution and fee terms. We then proposed $30 million; Brightline offered $28 million, which we accepted. Fees were discussed in the first proposal and remained at $2 million throughout; they were not deferred until after class relief was agreed. The settlement has no clear-sailing provision, and any fees the court does not award will go to the class rather than Brightline. We believe the settlement is fair to the class: its $28 million fund will be distributed automatically, without requiring claims, and provides recovery now despite substantial certification and trial risks and an estimated two-to-three-year wait for trial. The firm’s fixed compensation does not depend on the settlement or the fee award. The settlement remains subject to the court’s approval.
